method: 5 full-catalogue passes per model (`make eval-noise MODEL=… PASSES=5`), T2 sampling at temperature 0.2 with no seed. The contribution is computed by eval.contribution.floor_populations — the gate's OWN function — so what is measured is what is graded.
verdict: THE CALIBRATION FAILED, and that is the result. ADR 0021 prescribed sweeping a weak model as 'the single act that turns 30 into a calibrated number'. It was run. The distributions OVERLAP: the weak model's best pass (35) beats the default's worst (33), so no bar admits every pass of the default and rejects every pass of a model one third its size. min_contribution=30 sits below BOTH minima — against the only weak anchor we have it fails nothing. A 1B is not weak on this catalogue. The bar still catches a model contributing almost nothing (the null control scores 0/52 and fails it), but it cannot do what its name promises. The debt stays OPEN and the cheap remedy is ruled out.
rule_1_by_contrast: Rule 1 discriminates sharply on the same data: the weak model breaks 9 distinct floor runs to the default's 5, and more per pass. The rule anchored on the MEASURED FLOOR works; the rule with a CHOSEN NUMBER does not.

llama3.2:3b.role: the model the bar must ADMIT

llama3.2:1b.role: the model the bar must REJECT
